newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean ends up on short-covering.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean ends up on short-covering.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended up on Thursday on short-covering by retail investors, traders said.
The key November 1996 contract ended at 3,320 yuan ($400) per tonne, up two yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,300 and hit a high of 3,330.
January rose 19 to 3,229, March 24 to 3,234, May 104 to 3,350, July 30 to 3,350 and September 10 to 3,360.
Combined volume fell to 31,800 tonnes from 69,500.
Traders said short-covering by retail investors dominated today's trading.
"Some investors offset their positions and moved their money into more active markets," one trader said.
"Technical charts showed a possibility for further rises but did not breach the consolidation range," he added.
Traders said the potential for rises was greater than for falls but that the range will be limited in the next few days.
